A1.justification: Both nine-page PDFs describe the same TAAT and HumanML3D++ research. Text, equations, tables, and figures are readable throughout. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports original motion-generation experiments, dataset validation, and a Think-stage action-text accuracy analysis.

after.justification: v3 reports motion-generation experiments and dataset validation, plus new context-length ablation and comparative user-study results.

M1.justification: v2 explicitly avoids LLM fine-tuning and uses prompting. v3 instead trains the Think component using LoRA on scene/action question-answer pairs with token cross-entropy loss. This substantially changes a central component, while retaining the VQ-VAE and sequential motion-generation framework.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate HumanML3D action texts, HumanML3D++ scene texts, and transfer between them. Table 1 retains the same dataset sizes. The new user study and ablation do not establish additional task or data coverage.

E2.justification: The matched benchmark tables retain TM2T, MDM, MLD, MotionDiffuse, and T2M-GPT. However, v3 removes MotionDiffuse from the Figure 4 qualitative comparison and introduces a separate user-study comparison with T2M-GPT in Figure 5.

E3.justification: Scene-text evaluation replaces R-Precision/MM-Dist with threshold-based Hit Accuracy and minimum-over-N Mean Hit Distance. v2 instead documented ten action-text candidates and a ground-truth-based discriminator before motion generation. The reported transformer depth changes from 20 to 18 layers. v3 also introduces evaluation by 30 participants across five groups using 100 action texts and 100 scene texts.

E4.justification: v3 adds a sensitivity study of previous-action context lengths 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9 in Table 7, alongside human assessments of motion appropriateness. It removes v2's separate Think-stage diagnostic and Figure 6 match/similar/mismatch analysis. v3 Table 5 consolidates existing real-motion reference results rather than establishing a new experiment.

E5.justification: v3 newly displays error bars for user-study ratings in Figure 5, without explaining their statistical meaning. Retained benchmark metrics preserve their ± reporting, while the new Hit Accuracy and Mean Hit Distance scores have no uncertainty estimates. Neither version specifies benchmark run or seed counts.

E6.justification: v3 replaces scene retrieval scores with new hit-metric results and removes HumanML3D Top-1/Top-2 entries. TAAT reports Hit Accuracy/Mean Hit Distance of 79.9/1.075 in Table 2 and 75.1/1.212 in Table 4. Its HumanML3D++ FID changes from 0.448±0.006 to 0.379±0.014 under revised reported method/settings; most retained scores are identical. New ablation and user-study results are added. Real-motion FID in that comparison changes from 0.006 to 0.002, although v3 Table 5 retains 0.006.

T1.justification: v3 adds training-pair and token-loss formulations and mathematical definitions of the two new evaluation metrics. Existing VQ-VAE mathematics largely carries over. Its written sequence-likelihood product also drops conditioning on previous indices, despite retaining an autoregressive description. No new theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: v3 elevates the many-to-many evaluation problem into a central contribution, explicitly claiming a novel metric system in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. v2 foregrounded the dataset, framework, and scene understanding, describing a discriminator while acknowledging the need for better evaluation.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations involving feature-extractor degradation, discretization and independent sampling as sources of diversity, baseline dependence on ground-truth motion length, and context-length continuity/repetition tradeoffs. It removes v2's explicit concerns about insufficient scene annotations and the impracticality of LLM fine-tuning, substantially revising the mechanism and limitations discussion.

D1.justification: v3 omits settings including 64-frame tokenizer crops, tokenizer batch size 256 and EMA constant 0.99, minimum motion length, and detailed metric sampling counts. It newly discloses standardized training for dataset validators. Much of the codebook and transformer training recipe remains, and both versions only promise future code and dataset release.

R1.justification: Related work shifts from detailed Action2Motion/Text2Motion comparisons toward diffusion, transformer, and fine-grained generation limitations. v3 adds discussion of works including MoMask, HumanTOMATO, and FG-T2M, while removing treatments and citations such as PoseGPT, INR, and MotionGPT. This substantially changes research positioning beyond citation formatting.

P1.justification: The introduction and related work are extensively rewritten. Duplicated dataset material is consolidated, the standalone Discussion and Text2Action Accuracy sections disappear, and expanded evaluation, Ablation Study, and User Study sections reshape the narrative. Terminology and heading conventions also change throughout.

P2.justification: Figures 1–4 are extensively redesigned, including new character renderings and an expanded Think/Act/Test diagram. Benchmark tables are reordered and restructured. The FID chart becomes a difference table, the Think-stage pie chart disappears, and user-study and ablation displays are added. Document styling and figure placement change throughout.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful context-length and human-rating evidence and improves organization. However, it removes reproducibility details, leaves the new metrics' candidate count, threshold, and distance implementation unspecified, and does not explain how scene-pair LLM fine-tuning relates to its retained zero-shot claims. These uncertainties affect the newly central method and evaluation contributions, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall quality improvement.
